_about: Expert-curated insight cards per PSI investigation, written from the PSI investigation records (data/psi_details.json) and experiment tables. 'pillars' rate relevance 0-3 to NASA's fire safety pillars. Numeric condition ranges are NOT stored here; they are computed live from data/tests.csv.

investigations.name: BASS-II
investigations.full_name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
investigations.summary: Burned real spacecraft-type solids (PMMA films/slabs/cylinders, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric) in a slow, fan-driven air flow inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox, at normal and reduced oxygen levels.
what_varied: Material and geometry (films, slabs, rods/cylinders, spherical sections, fabric)
Flow speed (up to 40 cm/s) and direction (opposed, concurrent)
Oxygen concentration (lowered below 21% by adding nitrogen; 13.6 to 22.2% in the table)
held_constant: Small wind tunnel in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
measurements: Flame appearance, growth and spread rate from imaging
O2, CO2 and CO before and after each burn (table)
investigations.takeaway: Designed to bridge NASA's normal-gravity screening test (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) and actual microgravity flammability. Per the PSI approach, flame appearance, growth and spread rates were determined for realistic solids in opposed and concurrent flow up to 40 cm/s, with oxygen lowered below 21%. PSI states the results help engineers select the safest materials and improve firefighting methods.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: initial O2 and initial/final O2, CO2 and CO for 129 burns of realistic solids at reduced oxygen. Flame spread rates and extinction limits come from the imagery in the PSI data files, not the table.
investigations.habitat_note: The largest solid-material test set in PSI with varied oxygen (129 tests), but all at or below ~22% O2; extrapolating to 30%+ Moon-base air requires models.
investigations.earth_application: Material flammability standards, fire behaviour in enclosed and ventilated spaces (aircraft, submarines).
limitations: Flow reported as fan display, not calibrated cm/s, in the table
investigations.verified: PSI-25 objectives, approach and research impacts; BASS-II experiment table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: BASS
investigations.summary: ISS campaign burning practical solid fuels (SIBAL fabric, PMMA, Nomex, Ultem) in the glovebox flow duct, including wake flames and tests of an inert gaseous extinguishing agent.
what_varied: Flow speed (up to 40 cm/s) and direction (opposed, concurrent)
held_constant: 76 mm x 76 mm flow duct in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
measurements: Top- and edge-view video: flame size, shape and color
investigations.takeaway: Designed to relate the flammability of practical solids in microgravity to NASA's normal-gravity screening test, and to assess nitrogen (an inert agent similar to the one used on ISS) as an extinguishant across materials, geometries and flows. PSI states the results are used in first-order models of heat release and toward a performance-based material selection process.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: material and sample for 122 burns. Flame spread, quenching and radiometer data are in the PSI data files; baseline for BASS-II and Saffire.
investigations.habitat_note: Representative of ISS cabin air only.
investigations.earth_application: Fire behaviour behind obstructions (wake flames) in confined spaces.
limitations: O2 and pressure not varied (assumed cabin air)
Experiment table lists material and sample only
investigations.verified: PSI-26 objectives, approach and research impacts; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SAFFIRE-I
investigations.summary: A realistic, large-scale fire: a SIBAL fabric sample about 0.94 m x 0.4 m burned inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS.
what_varied: Flow direction: concurrent (sample S1) vs opposed (sample S2)
investigations.takeaway: Designed to determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low gravity and to compare low-g flammability with NASA's 1-g screening test. In the table, the fabric burned 420 s in concurrent flow versus 70 s in opposed flow.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: sample, flow, O2 and burn time. Fire growth, O2/CO2/pressure response and radiometer data for validating vehicle-level fire models are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Realistic, vehicle-scale fire data (together with Saffire-II and -III, the large-scale fire tests in PSI); directly relevant to spacecraft and rover cabin fire scenarios.
investigations.earth_application: Large-scale fire growth in confined vehicles.
investigations.verified: PSI-98 objectives, approach and research impacts; SAFFIRE-I table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SAFFIRE-II
investigations.summary: Nine smaller samples of different spacecraft materials (silicone, SIBAL, PMMA, Nomex) burned in Cygnus to compare microgravity flammability with the NASA 1-g screening test.
measurements: Burn length and spread rate in microgravity and in 1-g (table)
investigations.takeaway: In the table, flammability differed between 1-g and microgravity: thin silicone samples burned completely in 1-g tests but barely at all in microgravity, while SIBAL fabric burned its full 29 cm length in both. Designed to compare low-g flammability limits with NASA's 1-g screening test.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: microgravity and 1-g burn length and spread rate for the same materials (rare paired data); sensor time series are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Material screening insight for any crewed vehicle; still only cabin-air O2.
limitations: Small number of samples per material
investigations.verified: PSI-99 objectives and approach; SAFFIRE-II table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SAFFIRE-III
investigations.summary: Repeat of the large-scale fabric fire inside Cygnus at a higher flow speed (30 cm/s), in concurrent and opposed flow.
investigations.takeaway: Same objectives as Saffire-I (large-scale fire growth and low-g flammability), repeated at 30 cm/s instead of 20 cm/s in concurrent and opposed flow, giving a second flow speed for large-scale fabric fires.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: sample, flow and direction. Large-scale fire growth and atmosphere data at a second flow speed are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Realistic-scale fire, cabin air.
investigations.earth_application: Large-scale fire growth in confined vehicles.
investigations.verified: PSI-100 objectives and approach; SAFFIRE-III table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: FLEX
investigations.summary: Burned isolated methanol and heptane droplets to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels and measure how gaseous suppressants (CO2 and helium in the table) change them, over a range of oxygen levels and pressures.
measurements: Droplet burning rate and extinction diameter (droplet imaging)
Burn time and how each test ended (table)
investigations.takeaway: Designed to determine the limiting oxygen index (the lowest oxygen level that sustains burning) as a function of pressure, and how suppressants (CO2 and helium in the table) shift it. The table reports burning rate, extinction diameter and burn time for 274 tests: the inputs for choosing suppressant concentrations.
investigations.modeling_value: 274 individual tests with burning rate, extinction diameter and burn time; a core validation dataset for droplet combustion and suppression models.
investigations.habitat_note: Includes several tests above 30% O2 and below 1 atm, overlapping the planned Moon-base atmosphere; directly informs CO2 extinguisher sizing.
investigations.earth_application: Fire suppressant effectiveness, fuel efficiency and cool-flame chemistry for engines.
limitations: Liquid droplets, not solid cabin materials
Pressures about 0.7 to 3 atm: no tests at spacesuit pressure
investigations.verified: PSI-69 objectives and approach; FLEX experiment table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: FLEX-2
investigations.summary: Extended FLEX to practical and two-component fuels (heptane/iso-octane, propanol/glycerol), across pressures up to 3 atm and with slow imposed flow.
measurements: Color video of droplet and flame
investigations.takeaway: Designed to provide benchmark data on pure and two-component fuel droplets. The table lists the condition matrix: 0.5 to 3 atm, 17 to 30% O2 (the approach cites 10 to 40%), nitrogen or helium, and slow imposed flow.
investigations.modeling_value: Benchmark bi-component droplet data; the experiment table is a condition matrix (ranges), not per-test rows.
investigations.habitat_note: Covers O2 up to 30% and sub-atmospheric pressure, the edge of Moon-base conditions.
investigations.earth_application: Cleaner and more efficient liquid-fuel combustion.
limitations: Table gives ranges only; per-test values need the raw data
investigations.verified: PSI-68 objectives and approach; FLEX-2 experiment table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: CFI
investigations.summary: Studied low-temperature 'cool flames' of n-dodecane droplets at pressures from 0.5 to 5 atm, including helium dilution.
measurements: UV camera for OH* emission and flame size
investigations.takeaway: Cool flames are low-temperature reactions. CFI was designed to examine them for n-dodecane and blends from 0.25 to 5 atm, with helium dilution and different droplet sizes; PSI states it provides critical validation for chemical kinetic mechanisms and supports the design of safer spacecraft systems.
investigations.modeling_value: Low-temperature chemistry and cool-flame extinction limits vs pressure.
investigations.habitat_note: Pressure range brackets habitat pressures; O2 does not reach 30%.
investigations.verified: PSI-39 objectives, approach and research impacts; CFI experiment table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ACME CFI-G
investigations.full_name: ACME Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
investigations.summary: Gaseous cool flames (ethane, propane, butane in the table) on a spherical porous burner, in normal flames and inverse flames where oxygen-enriched gas up to 85% O2 flows out of the burner. Cool diffusion flames peak at only 500 to 1000 K.
held_constant: ACME spherical burner in the CIR
investigations.takeaway: In the table, O2 runs from 12 to 85%: the widest span of the 19 PSI combustion experiment tables (computed from all of them; ACME Flame Design also reaches 85%, from 19.8%), covering the 30%+ O2 expected in Moon bases and rovers. Designed to determine the conditions under which cool diffusion flames occur.
investigations.modeling_value: 333 tests with adiabatic flame temperature, stoichiometric mixture fraction and outcome; strong validation set for high-O2 kinetics.
investigations.habitat_note: Essential for Moon-base and rover atmospheres; note inverse-flame O2 is in the oxidizer stream, not the room air.
limitations: Gaseous fuels, not solid cabin materials
Inverse-flame O2 is not ambient O2
investigations.verified: PSI-159 objectives, approach and research impacts; CFI-G experiment tables; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ACME Flame Design
investigations.summary: Spherical ethylene flames (methane per the objectives; propane also appears in the table), normal and inverse, to find when flames start producing soot and when they extinguish, across dilution, flow rate and pressure.
investigations.takeaway: Designed to obtain soot-inception and extinction limits (radiative or kinetic) of spherical flames as functions of flow rate, mixture fraction, inert dilution and pressure. The tables list 327 tests with their conditions; soot governs how much heat a flame radiates.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: 327 tests with O2, pressure, flows and calculated flame temperature and mixture fraction. Soot-inception and extinction observations are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Covers elevated O2 and reduced pressure relevant to exploration atmospheres.
limitations: Inverse-flame O2 is in the burner stream
investigations.verified: PSI-10 objectives and approach; Flame Design experiment tables; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ACME BRE
investigations.summary: Used a gas-fed porous burner to emulate burning solids in still (quiescent) air. Its objectives list NASA's candidate exploration atmospheres (14.7 psia/21%, 10.2 psia/26.5%, 8.2 psia/34% O2); the table shows flames at 21, 25, 26.5, 34 and 40% O2.
investigations.takeaway: PSI reports that flames emulating burning PMMA and nylon kept burning steadily with no air flow in elevated-oxygen atmospheres, while similar flames at 21% O2 self-extinguished quickly. Since stopping ventilation is an established step in fighting spacecraft fires, turning off fans alone may not be enough at elevated oxygen. PSI notes these results are still preliminary.
investigations.modeling_value: Burning and extinction conditions expressed in terms of material properties: flammability maps that relate gas-burner flames to condensed (solid) fuels.
investigations.habitat_note: Its objectives list NASA's candidate exploration atmospheres, including 34% O2 at 8.2 psia, which is why it ranks first for Moon-base and rover atmospheres in this dashboard.
limitations: Pressure per test not in table
investigations.verified: PSI-20 objectives, approach and research impacts; BRE experiment table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ACME CLD Flame
investigations.summary: Weak, highly diluted methane and ethylene coflow flames to characterize lift-off, extinction and sooting at long residence times.
measurements: OH* and CH* chemiluminescence imaging (lift-off, flame shape)
Soot luminosity and laser extinction (soot temperature, volume fraction)
investigations.takeaway: Designed to provide data for rigorous testing of computational models at the extremes of fuel dilution: flame shape, lift-off height, temperatures, extinction limits and sooting of weak coflow flames.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: daily fuel, dilution range and flames ignited. Flame shape, lift-off, temperature and soot measurements for CFD validation are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Indirect: model validation rather than habitat conditions.
investigations.verified: PSI-21 objectives and approach; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
investigations.full_name: ACME Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
investigations.summary: Applied electric fields to coflow methane flames; the field pushes on ions in the flame, mimicking a weak buoyancy-like force.
measurements: Flame response time to electric forcing
investigations.takeaway: Applying an electric field pushes on the ions in a flame. The challenge brief notes that E-FIELD Flames used this effect to mimic partial gravity, making it a partial-gravity analog until lunar-gravity combustion data (LUCI, FM2) arrive.
investigations.modeling_value: Flame response to a controllable body-force analog.
investigations.habitat_note: Use with microgravity and 1-g data to bound Moon (1/6 g) and Mars (3/8 g) behaviour.
investigations.earth_application: Electric-field flame control to reduce soot and emissions.
limitations: PSI states the work was not conducted to serve space applications; the partial-gravity use comes from the challenge brief
investigations.verified: PSI-22 objectives, approach and research impacts; challenge brief; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ACME s-Flame
investigations.full_name: ACME Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
investigations.summary: Transient spherical diffusion flames of H2/CH4 and C2H4 mixtures to measure flame structure and extinction for model comparison.
investigations.takeaway: Designed to compare transient spherical flame structure and extinction limits with detailed numerical simulations, testing the transport and chemistry models that fire simulation codes rely on.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: daily fuel, atmosphere and flames ignited. Transient flame structure and extinction data are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Some tests at elevated O2.
investigations.verified: PSI-23 objectives and approach; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SPICE
investigations.summary: Measured the smoke point, the fuel flow at which a jet flame starts releasing soot, for ethylene, propane and propylene mixtures (methane also tested) at three burner diameters and co-flow speeds of 5.4 to 65 cm/s.
held_constant: MSG fan-driven flow duct (shared with BASS and SLICE)
measurements: Still and video cameras (flame length, soot emission)
investigations.takeaway: Per the PSI approach, fuel flow was adjusted to identify the smoke point (onset of soot emission) of non-buoyant flames for different fuels, burner sizes and co-flow speeds. PSI states this will improve understanding of soot formation and help design safer spacecraft environments.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: 469 flames with fuel, nozzle and co-flow rates. Smoke points and flame lengths are identified from the imagery in the PSI data files; input for soot models.
investigations.habitat_note: Cabin air only; informs smoke production for detection.
investigations.verified: PSI-107 objectives, approach and research impacts; SPICE table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SLICE
investigations.full_name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.summary: Studied the structure, stability and liftoff of jet flames in co-flowing air for methane, ethane and ethylene, with nitrogen dilution.
measurements: Pyrometry (calibration tests noted in the table)
investigations.takeaway: Designed to determine liftoff velocity limits and flame-base stability of jet flames in microgravity, and to validate numerical models of flame dynamics, soot and thermal radiation. PSI states the work gives insight into flame stability to enhance fire safety.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: test dates and fuels. Liftoff limits and flame structure are in the 4,000+ images in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Cabin air only.
limitations: Table lists only date and fuel
investigations.verified: PSI-106 objectives, approach and research impacts; SLICE table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SAME
investigations.summary: Overheated common spacecraft materials (Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, lampwick, dibutyl phthalate) to make smoke, then measured the smoke particle sizes in microgravity.
measurements: Thermophoretic samplers (particle size by electron microscopy)
Two smoke detectors (response from video record)
investigations.takeaway: PSI states SAME was intended to provide the reduced-gravity smoke baseline against which future spacecraft detector technology is evaluated, including quantitative data on how existing detectors respond to microgravity smoke.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: material, air flow, heating and aging settings. Smoke particle sizes (electron microscopy) and detector responses are in the PSI data files.
investigations.habitat_note: Applies to any closed habitat, where early smoke detection is critical.
limitations: Some sample grids contaminated (fixed in SAME-R)
investigations.verified: PSI-102 objectives, approach and research impacts; PSI-101 approach; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: SAME-R
investigations.summary: Reflight of SAME with a new material (Pyrell foam), higher heating temperatures, a no-flow condition and a new instrument (M-pass). PSI reports 66 flight test points; the table has 109 rows.
investigations.takeaway: Designed, like SAME, to relate smoke particle size to how smoke was generated and transported, with a new material, broader heating conditions and a new instrument. PSI states the results can lead to advanced fire-detector technology for future spacecraft.
investigations.modeling_value: Table: material, inlet velocity, heating duration, aging times and the Rt/R0 ratio as reported. Particle-size results are in the PSI data files and final report.
investigations.habitat_note: Applies to any closed habitat.
limitations: Particle sizes rely on a lognormal distribution assumption (checked in post-flight ground tests)
investigations.verified: PSI-101 objectives and approach; SAME-R table; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: DAFT / DAFT-2
investigations.full_name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.summary: Checked that the P-Trak particle counter used in SAME works in microgravity by measuring test dust and ISS cabin air.
investigations.takeaway: PSI reports the successful adaptation of the P-Trak particle counter (used by SAME) for microgravity, checked against a DustTrak, which underpins trust in SAME's smoke data. PSI notes it informs instruments for other challenging environments.
investigations.modeling_value: Instrument validation.
investigations.habitat_note: Lunar dust could trigger false smoke alarms, so detector selectivity matters on the Moon.
investigations.verified: PSI-47 objectives, approach and research impacts; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

investigations.name: ASE
investigations.summary: Collected airborne particles in ISS cabin air and returned them to Earth for analysis.
investigations.takeaway: PSI states the data can support the design and selection of particle detectors and air filtration suited to low gravity; background cabin aerosol is the 'normal' a smoke detector must distinguish from fire smoke.
investigations.modeling_value: Background aerosol levels.
investigations.habitat_note: Nuisance-alarm baseline for habitats.
investigations.verified: PSI-179 objectives, approach and research impacts; reviewed again to separate stated objectives from reported results

ground_studies.summary: Derived temperature and soot volume fraction fields from SPICE flame images.
New flamelet-manifold CFD model for concurrent flame spread over solids, validated with BASS-II-type data.
Simulated how gravity changes smoke particle growth, using SAME data.
3-D OpenFOAM model of droplet cool flames under heating and drift, validated with FLEX.
Cool-flame flammability-limit diagram from counterflow experiments and FLEX data.
